utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-83-PT, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I take the appearances. From the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, counsel, and to everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin and Daryl Mundis, assisted by our case manager Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, good morning to our colleagues from the OTP. I am Vasvija Vidovic. I appear for the Defence of General Rasim Delic. Together with me is Mr. Geoff Roberts, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. There are several outstanding motions. I will deal with those, but before that I would like to go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the two most important motions of the outstanding motions would be the Defence motion alleging defects in the form of the indictment and the Prosecution motion seeking leave to amend the indictment. Originally I anticipated the Chamber would be able to issue a decision on the Defence motion challenging the form of the indictment so that the Prosecution could incorporate any suggestions from the Chamber, if any, into the proposal to seek the leave to amend the indictment. However, it turned out not to be the case, and we have to sort out a way to deal with these two motions in an appropriate order and manner. According to my observation, the new indictment, if I can call the proposed amendment that way, into three parts. The first one would be the addition of new charges or crime bases under the count of murder and cruel treatment. And the second part would be the addition edited parts of the current indictment as the Prosecution had indicated in the response to the Defence motion as it -- as it would do so. And the third part will be the remaining parts which remain the same as before. So could I propose to the parties not to deal with the second and third parts for the moment. That is, the Chamber will consider, first of all, the -- whether to allow the addition of charges. So if the leave was granted, we'll deal with the form of -- the challenge on the form of the indictment altogether, and then if rejected, then we'll deal -- the Chamber will make a decision on the motion which is outstanding in relation to the previous indictment. But I understand there's an issue in relation to the supporting materials for this proposed amendment, and the Chamber has been briefed on the position of the Prosecutor as well as the Defence, but the Chamber made its position very clear in earlier cases. So the Chamber issued a decision in the case of Stanisic and Simatovic on 15th of June this year where it was -- the Prosecution was ordered to disclose the supporting materials to the Defence. So the Chamber deliberated on this matter, so it can be so ordered. For the record, I cite two paragraphs from the earlier decision: "Considering that after the confirmation of the indictment there are no provisions in the Rules or Statute of the International Tribunal that require or permit the supporting materials to be filed ex parte while the Rule explicitly provides that the parties shall be heard. Considering further that to give efficacy to the right of the Defence to be heard on the Rule 50(A)(i)(c) by enabling it to consider whether the proposed amendment might cause unfair prejudice to the accused, it must be furnished with all the material supporting the proposed amendment and that, should there be need for any such material to be given protection, the Prosecution may apply for such protection." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. For those reasons, the Chamber ordered the Prosecution to disclose supporting material to the Defence subject to protective measure, if necessary, and it is so ordered here on behalf of the Chamber. Can I ask, Mr. Mundis, whether, having said that, whether you need any kind of protective measures in relation to that. And can I ask when you can complete this disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding at this point in time is that there are a few examples of material that was taken from other cases that is subject to, for example, private-session testimony or perhaps even exhibits that were tendered under seal. We will review that material on an expedited basis and inform the Trial Chamber or make a filing as quickly as possible as to which material would require continuing protective measures from previous rulings. There may also be some material that was covered by Rule 70. We'll have to take a full examination, but I don't anticipate that would take a significant period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think you need a decision from the Chamber for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would -- we would certainly, however, Your Honour, call to the Chamber's attention and to the attention of the Defence that material which is subject to protective measures in other proceedings. Whether or not we need an order from the Chamber, we feel it's our responsibility to call to the attention of the Defence and to the Trial Chamber that material which is covered by protective measures in other proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So can I ask you here that -- to disclose them as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will so do, Your Honour. If I could take this opportunity, my case manager a moment ago also drew to my attention that the version of the indictment which was -- or proposed amended indictment which was filed contained again, under counts 3 and 4, the identities of the victims, which Your Honour is well aware the public version of that material has been filed in a redacted format. So we would ask again if the confidential nature of the proposed amended indictment is released, either the Registry redact the identity of those individuals, or that we be permitted to substitute the redacted version pursuant to the earlier order that allowed us to protect the identities of those victims listed under counts 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I assume the Defence would have no opposition as for the protective measures vis-a-vis it's public, but their concern may be whether there should be delayed disclosure to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The identities of these victims is known to the Defence, and the statements of these witnesses have been disclosed to the Defence. Our concern at this point in time is the public -- the revelation in public of the identities of these victims listed in counts 3 and 4, and Your Honour will recall that previously we had asked that pseudonyms be used in place of their names in the public version of the indictment. And so to amend what I said earlier in terms of our willingness to consent to lifting the confidential nature of the proposed amended indictment, we would ask that prior to that proposed amended indictment being released to the public, that either the Registry redact the identities of those individuals or that we be permitted to substitute the redacted version with respect to the identity of those three named victims under counts 3 and 4 so that that not be put into the public domain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should have been so noted by the Defence as well as the registrar. Thank you. So then that said, the Defence would be required to file its response as to the issue of addition of new charges only in 14 days from the receipt of the supporting material.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. And afterwards, after the Chamber will issue the decision as to the addition of new charges, the Chamber will consider the issue of challenge on the form of the indictment, if any. So if the Defence -- this is the case when the amendment was -- leave to amend the indictment was granted -- would be granted. If the Defence is going to file a challenge on the amended indictment, I would like to request the Defence to incorporate all the submissions submitted in the previous filing into the new motion so thereby replacing the old motion for the convenience of the Chamber to consider the matter. Could you do that, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic. There's one matter for which I would like to ask a clarification from the Prosecution, which arose in the course of the deliberation of the Chamber on the issue of the challenge on the form of the indictment, and that is related to the character of the conflict pleaded in the indictment. One of the challenge of the Defence is that character of the armed conflict has not been specifically pleaded in the indictment, whether it is an international armed conflict or internal armed conflict, and the Prosecution's response is that in the case of Article 3, the character of the armed conflict is not a material fact, and I can -- in a general sense I can understand that, but in one of the paragraphs -- is it paragraph 17? Let me check. I think it's paragraph 10. There's a mention of the alleged involvement of the army of the Republic of Croatia, HV. So my question is: Why do you need that passage? In other words, whether the Prosecution intends to establish any commission of any offences for which an international armed conflict nexus is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The simple answer is no, and that's another reason in conjunction with our position with respect to Article 3 and the charges in this indictment, that we don't need to characterise the armed conflict as being either international or non-international, and that is a position that is, I believe, consistent throughout the pleadings of the OTP. I simply add also, Your Honour, that in -- it is possible that evidence will be led during the course of the trial that at least mentions the involvement of the HV, and we took the position that we should Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. specifically insert that so as to avoid any potential problems later as to the relevance of why evidence or witnesses were testifying about the involvement of the HV. And so it's not necessarily a fact that is -- that is absolutely critical or crucial to the Prosecution case, but on the other hand, we do anticipate that evidence will be not necessarily led but will be put before the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's nothing to do with the material facts of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So can I take it that the Prosecution wouldn't mind if the Chamber would order to take out that passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, again our position would be that if we -- if we were then precluded from any evidence being led, whether it was intentional or whether a witness simply blurted out that the HV was involved in the armed conflict, we would not want that evidence necessarily to be stricken from the record for the simple reason that the Defence said there's no reference to the HV in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question is this: If that is not a material fact, why would the Prosecution need that kind of evidence at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, we -- about all I can say at this point, Your Honour, is that we have had similar issues arise in a number of other cases where witnesses, in answering questions on their own have, in effect, blurted out the presence of foreign armed forces in the territory of Bosnia, and that has in some cases presented difficulties when the parties then objected or asked that that material be excluded. So it was simply put in there in an abundance of caution so that in the event any witnesses were to testify, or there were to be any documents that mentioned the presence of HV units on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the relevant time period, that that evidence would be part of the overall context in which the alleged crimes took place. So it could be part of the overall context in which the crimes, particularly in Central Bosnia, occurred and took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I assumed that it may be related to overall Prosecution position as to the nature of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So did I make it clear that after the -- if the decision granting the amendment be issued, the Defence would file preliminary motions, if any, in 30 days. A comprehensive one replacing the previous one. Thank you. And one -- another minor matter in relation to the amendment. Annex B is a so-called red-line version, but I don't think it reflects all the changes in the new indictment. Give me a minute. So let us, for example, take paragraph 17 of the new indictment. It says it added -- did you find it, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It added "From 8th of June, 1993 until 12th of January, 1995," which is not reflected here, and the "307th Motorised Brigade" is a replacement for the previous text which is "7th Muslim Mountain Brigade." So to the reader it is not clear how it was changed. So if you -- the Prosecution could file, replace the Annex B with the so-called red-line version or "track change" version later on, it would assist the Chamber as well as the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And -- thank you, Mr. Mundis. There are other several motions. For example, Defence motion seeking access to all confidential material in Kordic and Blaskic cases. And also there's Prlic's motion for access to all confidential material in Delic. The Chamber will consider these matters and issue its decision in due course. But could I ask Ms. Vidovic whether the Defence is minded to respond to the Prlic's motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask the parties whether there's anything to raise in relation to the issue of disclosure. Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't have anything at this point in time to add to what was said at the 65 ter meeting. Disclosure is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Yesterday, we met with the Prosecutor, and we submitted a letter to him. We're still working on that, so we have nothing at present. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any other matters to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give me a minute. Can I see the legal officer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday I promised that I would give an answer to a question, namely why we filed a motion for access to confidential material in the Blaskic case to Trial Chamber III. What we bore in mind was this was a different procedure according to 75(G)(ii). However, it's no problem. We can send it to another Trial Chamber, too, but it was my assumption that there was a different procedure involved before Trial Chamber III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think there is no Trial Chamber seized of the first proceeding, so I think it is this Chamber, seized of the second proceeding, to deal with the matter. So there are no further matters. This hearing is adjourned.
